title: Terrain signatures in Welsh settlement names
abstract: arXiv:2608.26978v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Landscapes are named, but whether names retain measurable environmental information beyond broad geographic structure is rarely tested. We analysed 3,757 Welsh settlements using a frozen, source-audited 24-element lexical framework, preregistered outcome-specific models and geographically structured validation. The central comparison contrasted 101 settlements carrying high-terrain elements (\textit{bryn} or \textit{mynydd}) with 139 carrying low-terrain elements (\textit{cwm} or \textit{pant}). High-terrain names occupied locations 24.4 m higher relative to their 2-km surroundings (95\% CI, 10.8--38.1 m; Holm-adjusted $p$ = 0.00137). The association remained positive across prespecified 1-, 2- and 5-km neighbourhood definitions and was reproduced using an independently produced elevation source (24.1 m; 95\% CI, 10.6--37.6 m). Adding terrain-name polarity to a non-lexical spatial and settlement baseline reduced geographically held-out

translated_title: 威尔士聚落名称中的地形特征
translated_abstract: 景观被命名，但名称是否保留超越广泛地理结构的可测量环境信息，很少被测试。我们使用一个冻结的、来源审计的24元素词汇框架、预注册的结果特定模型和地理结构化验证，分析了3,757个威尔士聚落。核心比较对比了101个带有高地地形元素（如“bryn”或“mynydd”）的聚落与139个带有低地地形元素（如“cwm”或“pant”）的聚落。高地地形名称的聚落相对于其2公里周围环境高出24.4米（95%置信区间，10.8--38.1米；霍尔姆校正p = 0.00137）。该关联在预指定的1、2和5公里邻域定义中保持正向，并使用独立生成的高程源进行了复制（24.1米；95%置信区间，10.6--37.6米）。将地形名称极性添加到非词汇空间和聚落基线中，减少了地理保持验证的误差。
tldr: 本研究首次通过严格验证的词汇框架和地理结构化模型，证明威尔士聚落名称中的地形词汇（如“bryn”与“cwm”）能可靠地反映局部海拔差异，表明地名保留了可量化的环境信息。
en_tdlr: This study demonstrates, through rigorously validated lexical frameworks and geographically structured models, that terrain-related words in Welsh settlement names (e.g., "bryn" vs. "cwm") reliably reflect local elevation differences, indicating place names retain measurable environmental information.
